title: Pollution, Isotonic Nasal Wash, NSAID Evaluation
official: Pollution, Isotonic Nasal Wash, NSAID Evaluation (PINE)
summary:
The goal of this clinical exposure study is to investigate the inflammatory and airway responses to controlled wood smoke exposure, a model for wildfire-related air pollution, and how these responses change with Otrivin Natural Saline Nasal Spray and Advil Extra Strength Liqui-Gels 400mg, used within their approved indications for clearing the nasal passages and the relief of pain and inflammation, respectively, in healthy adult participants. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How does controlled wood smoke exposure affect airway inflammation, and how does this response change with Advil use?
* How do the nasal effects of wood smoke exposure change with Otrivin Natural saline nasal spray use? Researchers will compare the effects of wood smoke exposure and these interventions versus filtered air and placebo using a crossover design, where each participant will be compared to themselves. Participants will complete questionnaires, breathing tests, nasal sampling and blood collections before and after each exposure.
conditions: This Study Will Evaluate the Effects of Woodsmoke Exposures and Advil in Healthy Adults
